subsystem_notes.note: Audited lib/report/report.py (create_nms_device_nodes, create_nms_report, run_report, label_ccu_coach_devices, map_to_physical_coach_numbers, get_painted_coach_id, parse_version_string, normalise_devices, generate_device_mqtt_events, compare_json) plus lib/report/device.py and the DOSTO walk in lib/report/report_dosto_neu.py. The dominant consumer-impact pattern is the BFS-only coach numbering: only devices reached and correctly numbered by the primary topology walk survive normalise_devices(); every other discovered-but-unnumbered device is silently dropped from device_instances and therefore from the consist payload AND from the MQTT add/remove diff. Because the same self.device_instances feeds both the consist topic and the device_added/device_removed event diff, drops and transient discovery misses cascade into NMS showing devices missing and flapping. Several field-level issues (paintedCoachId, firmware/config/serial 'unknown', macAddr/ipAddr casing) also push wrong/stale values to NMS.

Audited the MQTT change/event surface in lib/report/report.py (compare_json ~102, store_report ~137, create_nms_device_nodes ~191, generate_device_mqtt_events ~433, generate_uptime_mqtt_events ~458, run_report ~608) plus the Device equality/serialization contract (lib/report/device.py) and the discovery producer (backbone_discovery.py:80-95) that feeds output_file. The dominant defect class is FLAP: OBN compares exactly ONE fresh discovery snapshot against the last published snapshot, keyed purely by MAC, with no debounce/multi-sample confirmation. A single SNMP timeout in a cycle therefore propagates straight to consumers as device_removed (and next cycle device_added) and drops the device from obn/consist. The second class is STALE SUPPRESSION: compare_json's notion of 'changed' is driven by Device dataclass compare=True fields, which deliberately EXCLUDE coach_number/device_number/type/physical_coach_number — so a real change to coach numbering or painted-coach label, with other fields unchanged, makes compare_json return False and the corrected topology is never republished, leaving NMS permanently stale. memory is compare=True (device.py:16) which would cause per-cycle churn, but discovery never emits a 'memory' key so it is latent, not active — excluded. enable_mqtt/only_send_as_master gating is sound.

Audited lib/zabbix.py (ZabbixGenerator.generate_nodes/generate_coach_nodes/get_painted_coach_number, ZabbixChecker.check, load_discovered_consist), zabbix_generate.py, zabbix_check.py, plus tests/lib/test_zabbix.py and DOSTO discovery fixtures. The dominant, fleet-wide defect is that the LLD coach count is bounded by max(coach_number) over discovered devices, so a trailing coach whose devices all fail to be numbered (coach_number=None, the device.py default for a walk miss) is silently dropped from Zabbix discovery — the classic 'consumer sees device missing' pattern, here at coach granularity. Second fleet-wide issue: {#PAINTED_COACH_NUMBER} is always 'UNKNOWN' for DOSTO because physical_coach_number is never present in DOSTO discovery snapshots. Coach-0 master coaches (ACE/ccjpa) are also structurally excluded by the falsy guard plus range-from-1. The LLD is template-driven (consist.yaml), not discovery-driven, so it advertises the expected grid rather than what was actually found.

confirmed.title: Unnumbered discovered devices are dropped from the consist payload, so NMS shows them missing
confirmed.claim: normalise_devices() rebuilds self.device_instances keeping only devices where coach_number, device_number and type are all non-None. Any device the primary topology walk (number_coaches) reached but could not assign a coach/device number to — e.g. a switch whose uplink lands on an unexpected port, or an AP on a port other than E0-4/E1-2 in report_dosto_neu.py lines 76-156 — is silently deleted. create_nms_device_nodes() (line 197) only iterates the surviving device_instances, so the device never appears in obn/consist. The device is discovered and reachable but invisible to NMS.
confirmed.trigger: A real device whose physical cabling/port does not match the hard-coded walk rules (mis-cabled coupler, AP on an unexpected port, a switch the BFS could not number) is discovered but left with coach_number/device_number=None.
confirmed.consumer_symptom: NMS renders the train diagram and inventory with the device absent (reads as missing/down), even though OBN discovered it and it is online.

verdict.reasoning:
The drop path is statically provable end-to-end for the DostoNeu (4736/4734/4705 NEU) report.

1. report_dosto_neu.py number_coaches() (lines 53-159) BFS-walks from the CCU. coach_number/device_number default to None (Device dataclass, device.py:22-23). They are set ONLY when the neighbour's port matches a hard-coded rule: an AP gets coach_number set unconditionally (line 80) but device_number ONLY on E0_4 or (SW3 + E1_2) (lines 82-86); a SW gets both numbers set only inside one of the matching elif branches (lines 88-155). A device reached on any other port (mis-cabled coupler, AP on an unexpected port, a switch the BFS could not number) is still appended to the queue (line 158) but left with coach_number/device_number = None.

2. Line 162 calls normalise_devices(), which at report.py:254-260 rebuilds self.device_instances keeping ONLY devices where coach_number, device_number AND type are all non-None — silently deleting the unnumbered device. Comment line 161/253: "Remove any devices that were not detected properly (switch on wrong ports etc.)".

3. create_nms_device_nodes() (report.py:191-235) iterates only the surviving self.device_instances; run_report() calls number_coaches() (line 624) then create_nms_device_nodes() (line 631) and publish_consist_to_mqtt() → topic obn/consist (line 639). So the dropped device never appears in the consist payload to NMS.

NO upstream guard: there is no None-tolerant inclusion, and DostoNeu's walk does not even call report_unexpected_connection() (which report_ace/dsb/generic/queensland/tgv2020 do) — so for DOSTO the drop is fully silent (only normalise_devices emits a DEBUG line). The only related safeguard, lib/validate/validate.py test_unnumbered_devices() (lines 197-216), is a separate engineer-run `obn validate` diagnostic that merely flags discovered-but-unreported devices; its own docstring confirms the behaviour ("devices that didn't get a coach number assigned, are left out of the report JSON"). It does not re-include the device in obn/consist, so it does not prevent the NMS symptom. only_send_as_master (line 637) gates whether the report publishes at all, not which devices are in it.

The trigger (a device on an unexpected port) is real-world plausible — exactly the mis-cabled-coupler / wrong-port-AP / un-numberable-switch scenarios this fleet hits (CLAUDE.md misimaged-switches, coupler cable-swap notes). Marking confirmed because the code path is statically certain; the only data-dependence is whether such a device is physically present.
verdict.covered_by_test: tests/lib/report/test_report_dosto_neu.py::TestDostoNeuReport::test_number_coaches is the only test on this path. It is a HAPPY-PATH test: fixtures discovery_nv6.prev.json (43 devices) and discovery_nv4_2_coaches.json (15 devices) contain only well-formed, fully-numberable devices (verified: zero devices with null coach/device_number). It strips type/coach/device then asserts number_coaches() reproduces the exact expected set (device_nodes == expected_result). It never includes a mis-cabled/unexpected-port device, so it neither exercises nor refutes the drop behaviour. No test asserts that unnumbered devices are retained. validate.py test_unnumbered_devices has tests but they cover the validate diagnostic, not the consist payload.
verdict.consumer_impact: On any DOSTO NEU train (4736-/4734-/4705- series, train_type nv4/nv6/fv5/fv6) where a real, online, discovered device sits on a port the hard-coded walk does not expect (mis-cabled inter-coach/coupler link, AP not on E0-4/E1-2, or a switch the BFS cannot number), that device is dropped from the obn/consist MQTT payload. NMS then renders the train diagram and device inventory with that device absent — it reads as missing/down even though OBN discovered it and ICMP/SNMP to it succeed. Zabbix, which is provisioned from discovery, is unaffected for that host directly, but the NMS consist/topology view and painted-coach mapping will under-count the consist. Trains with correct cabling (the common case) are unaffected — only mis-cabled or non-standard-port consists show the symptom, which makes it easy to misread as a hardware/cabling fault rather than an OBN reporting gap. The silent nature is aggravated for DOSTO specifically because report_dosto_neu does not even log report_unexpected_connection.

confirmed.title: Dropped devices also generate a spurious device_removed MQTT event
confirmed.claim: generate_device_mqtt_events() computes removed_macs = previous - current using self.device_instances (post-normalise, drop-filtered) vs previous_instances. A device that was numbered (and present) on a prior run but, on this run, the walk fails to number (so normalise_devices drops it) shows up as a removed MAC and emits obn/event/device_removed even though the device is still physically present and discovered. The next successful run re-numbers it and emits device_added. This is the same drop-cascade as the consist-topic finding but on the event stream.
confirmed.trigger: Any run where a transient discovery/LLDP miss or a one-off port mismatch causes a previously-numbered device to fail numbering this cycle.
confirmed.consumer_symptom: NMS sees device_removed then device_added — the device flaps out of and back into the inventory in MongoDB, generating false remove/add churn.

verdict.reasoning: Statically provable. generate_device_mqtt_events() (report.py:433-449) computes removed_macs = set(old_devices.keys()) - set(new_devices.keys()) where new_devices = self.device_instances and old_devices = self.previous_instances, then fires obn/event/device_removed for each removed MAC at lines 445-449. Critically, self.device_instances is the POST-normalise set: in run_report() (lines 623-641) the order is load_json() -> number_coaches() -> ... -> generate_device_mqtt_events(). number_coaches() (e.g. report_dosto_neu.py:31-162) ends with self.normalise_devices(), which at report.py:254-260 hard-drops every device whose coach_number/device_number/type is None. The numbering is a BFS over LLDP neighbour ports (report_dosto_neu.py:53-158); a transient LLDP miss or a one-off wrong port reading leaves a physically-discovered device unnumbered, so normalise_devices drops it from device_instances even though it is present in raw discovery (output_file). self.previous_instances is loaded from cfg.report_file (lines 88-91), which store_report() (lines 137-141) wrote from the prior run's already-normalised device_instances. So the diff is last-run-survivors minus this-run-survivors: a device that numbered last cycle but fails to number this cycle appears in removed_macs and emits device_removed; the next clean cycle re-numbers it and emits device_added (lines 440-443). No upstream guard exists: there is no None/unnumbered filter, no check against raw discovery, and no presence test inside generate_device_mqtt_events. The only gate (only_send_as_master at line 637) gates the whole MQTT block but does not distinguish genuine removal from a normalise drop, so on the master CCU the spurious event fires. compare_json() (lines 102-135) only decides whether to send at all; a size change (one fewer device) returns True, so the event path is reached. The claimed mechanism is therefore exactly what the code does.
verdict.covered_by_test: tests/lib/report/test_report.py::TestMqttEvents::test_device_removed (lines 1310-1319) and test_multple_removed (1335-1347). These confirm rather than refute the claim: test_device_removed sets previous_instances=[dev_one,dev_two,dev_three], device_instances=[dev_one,dev_two] and asserts publish_to_mqtt is called once with obn/event/device_removed for dev_three. The test treats any MAC present in previous but absent from current as a removal and fires the event — it has no notion of "dropped by failed numbering vs physically gone," which is precisely the unguarded behaviour the claim describes. No test asserts the opposite (i.e. no test feeds a still-discovered-but-unnumbered device and asserts device_removed is suppressed).
verdict.consumer_impact: NMS (MongoDB inventory fed by the obn/event/* topics) sees a device_removed immediately followed by device_added on the next clean OBN report cycle — the affected switch/AP flaps out of and back into the inventory, producing false remove/add churn and any downstream alarm/notification tied to device inventory changes. Scope: any DOSTO-NEU train (nv4/nv6/fv5/fv6 via report_dosto_neu/report_generic number_coaches paths) running on the master CCU during a cycle where a previously-numbered device transiently fails numbering (LLDP miss / one-off port mismatch). It is data/runtime-dependent in frequency (needs a transient numbering failure to actually occur) but the code path itself is statically guaranteed to emit the spurious event when that condition is met. Distinct from (not a duplicate of) the consist-topic drop finding: same root cause (normalise drop) but a different MQTT topic and consumer path (obn/event/device_removed vs obn/consist).

confirmed.title: paintedCoachId falls back to 'unknown' for an entire coach when its switch is unmapped or dropped
confirmed.claim: get_painted_coach_id(coach_number) scans device_instances for any device in that coach with physical_coach_number not None and returns it, else 'unknown'. physical_coach_number is only ever set on type=='SW' devices (map_to_physical_coach_numbers, line 324) and only when the MAC is present in the physical_coach_map file (get_physical_coach_number, line 337). If a coach's switch was dropped by normalise, or that switch's MAC is missing from physical_coach_map_file, then EVERY device in that coach (APs, BOX, etc.) gets paintedCoachId='unknown' in the NMS node even though they are correctly coach-numbered.
confirmed.trigger: physical_coach_map_file lacks an entry for a coach's switch MAC, or the coach's only switch was dropped by the walk; common when the map file is unmaintained.
confirmed.consumer_symptom: NMS shows 'unknown' painted coach number for all devices in that coach, mislabeling the customer-facing coach identity.

verdict.reasoning: Code at report.py:339 reads exactly as cited: get_painted_coach_id(coach_number) scans device_instances for any device where coach_number matches AND device.physical_coach_number is not None, returning that value, else 'unknown'. physical_coach_number is ONLY set on type=='SW' devices (map_to_physical_coach_numbers, lines 321-327) and ONLY when the MAC is present in the loaded physical_coach_map (get_physical_coach_number, line 337: self.physical_coach_map.get(mac, None)). If physical_coach_map_file is unset, the map defaults to {} (line 335), so every MAC misses and EVERY device gets 'unknown'. If set but a coach's switch MAC is absent (unmaintained map), only that coach's devices get 'unknown'. The NMS output path is direct and unguarded: create_nms_device_nodes (line 200) writes new_node['paintedCoachId'] = self.get_painted_coach_id(device.coach_number) for EVERY device unconditionally — no None filter, no only_send_as_master gate on the field (the only_send_as_master gate at line 637 governs whether to publish at all, not the field value), no fallback to coachId. run_report calls map_to_physical_coach_numbers (line 626) then create_nms_device_nodes (line 631), confirming the order. A dropped switch: normalise_devices (lines 253-260) removes devices lacking coach_number/device_number/type, so a coach whose only SW was dropped (or whose SW MAC is unmapped) has no numbered SW carrying a physical_coach_number, while surviving APs/BOX in that coach still emit. NO upstream guard exists. This is statically provable AND codified as the intended contract by green tests.
verdict.covered_by_test: tests/lib/report/test_report.py::test_get_painted_coach_id (line 470) directly asserts the behavior: coach 1 (SW with physical_coach_number)->'coach1', coach 2 (device with coach_number but NO physical_coach_number)->'unknown', coach 3->'coach3'. Additionally, tests/lib/report/test_report_ccjpa_wd2.py::test_create_device_nodes (line 187, parametrized over no_icl/obn_134/with_box) builds the NMS device nodes WITHOUT calling map_to_physical_coach_numbers and asserts equality against fixtures (tests/resources/ccjpa-wd2/target_nms_report_no_icl.json, target_nms_report_obn_134.json, target_nms_report_with_box.json) in which EVERY device's paintedCoachId == 'unknown'. These are green tests asserting exactly the claimed fall-through, not refuting it.
verdict.consumer_impact: In the NMS MQTT consist message (messageInfo HYBRID_CONSIST_V1), the paintedCoachId field for every device (SW, AP, ICL, BOX) in an affected coach is the literal string 'unknown' instead of the customer-painted coach number — while coachId (the positional/logical number) remains correct. NMS shows 'unknown' as the painted/customer-facing coach identity for those devices. Scope is entirely data-dependent on the per-train physical_coach_map_file: if that file is unset for a fleet (the DOSTO-NEU/OBB default — no physical_coach_map_file configured), ALL coaches on ALL such trains show paintedCoachId='unknown' (consistent with the painted-coach-number-source gap already noted in memory: chain unset on DOSTO-NEU -> 'unknown'); if the file is set but stale/missing a switch MAC, only the coach(es) whose switch MAC is absent (or whose switch was dropped by normalise) are mislabeled, and only on those specific trains. It does not affect Zabbix port/firmware polling or device reachability — purely a cosmetic/identity label in the NMS consist view.

confirmed.title: macAddr is force-uppercased but ipAddr is passed through unchanged — case-sensitive identity mismatch risk for consumers
confirmed.claim: create_nms_device_nodes() emits macAddr as device.mac.upper() (line 205) while find_ap() (line 483) and generate_device_mqtt_events() key by the raw, un-uppercased device.mac. The NMS payload's macAddr casing therefore differs from the casing OBN uses internally and in the MQTT event payloads (as_dict() emits the raw mac). A consumer that joins consist nodes to device_added/device_removed events by MAC string will see case-mismatched keys (e.g. 'A0:59:3A:..' in consist vs 'a0:59:3a:..' in events).
confirmed.trigger: Discovery records a MAC in lowercase (typical); consist node uppercases it, event payload does not.
confirmed.consumer_symptom: NMS correlating the consist topic against device_added/device_removed/device_changed by MAC may fail to match the same physical device, treating the consist entry and the event entry as different devices.

verdict.reasoning: Static facts verified in report.py (origin/master, src/usr/share/obn/lib/report/). Line 204 emits ipAddr=device.ip (passthrough), line 205 emits macAddr=device.mac.upper() in create_nms_device_nodes(), which builds the obn/consist topic payload (publish_consist_to_mqtt, line 639). device.mac is stored LOWERCASE: parsers.py parse_mac_address() returns value...lower() (line 29), and test_report.py line 168 asserts the device-list mac stays lowercase (94:9b:2c:29:62:34). The divergent path is generate_device_mqtt_events() (lines 433-456): obn/event/device_added/removed/changed payloads are json.dumps(...as_dict()), and report/device.py as_dict() (lines 47-53) serializes __dict__ verbatim, so it emits key "mac" with the RAW lowercase value and a different key NAME than the consist node's "macAddr". Both are published in the same run (lines 639-641). No upstream guard normalizes casing between the two output paths. So the consist projection and the event stream disagree on MAC casing (uppercase vs lowercase) AND key name (macAddr vs mac). The claim is correct on the core divergence but WRONG on one cited detail: find_ap() (line 483) joins by IP (device_instance.ip == device_node["ipAddr"]), not by raw mac — it is an internal lookup, not a consumer correlation key, so it neither supports nor refutes; the real second source of the raw mac is as_dict() in the MQTT events. The mismatch is deterministic (independent of discovery data values), hence statically provable rather than runtime-dependent.
verdict.covered_by_test: Both casings are independently locked in by GREEN tests, which proves the divergence is real and intended on each side rather than an incidental bug: (1) consist/NMS uppercase — tests/resources/ccjpa-wd2/target_nms_report_obn_134.json and tests/resources/queensland/nms_report_with_devices_expected.json assert macAddr in UPPERCASE (e.g. 94:9B:2C:29:62:34) from lowercase source, asserted by test_report.py TestReport NMS-conversion tests; (2) MQTT event lowercase — tests/lib/report/test_report.py::TestMqttEvents::test_device_added (line 1308) asserts the obn/event/device_added payload equals json.dumps(dev_three) where dev_three={"mac":"aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:03",...} i.e. lowercase key "mac". No single test asserts cross-topic case consistency, so nothing guards against the divergence.
verdict.consumer_impact: OBN publishes two MQTT projections per discovery cycle on every DOSTO-NEU CCU: obn/consist (field macAddr, UPPERCASE) and obn/event/device_{added,removed,changed} (field mac, lowercase). A consumer that correlates a consist node to a device lifecycle event by a case-sensitive MAC string comparison would treat them as different devices. However, two facts cap the real-world severity at low: (a) the two payloads use different KEY names anyway (macAddr vs mac), so any consumer reading both already maps fields explicitly rather than blindly string-joining; (b) within OBN there is no MAC-keyed cross-topic join — find_ap joins consist-to-instance by IP, not MAC. Whether the ÖBB NMS actually does a case-sensitive MAC join across these two topics is NMS-side and not visible in this repo, so the concrete NMS/Zabbix-visible breakage cannot be confirmed from OBN alone; if NMS normalizes case (common) there is zero impact. Scope, if it bites, is fleet-wide (all DOSTO trains, every cycle), but presents only as event-vs-consist de-duplication noise, not as a health/connectivity fault.

confirmed.title: No confirmation/hysteresis on device add/remove diff - any one-cycle absence is published immediately
confirmed.claim: Independent of the discovery-degradation path, generate_device_mqtt_events() (report.py:433-449) takes added_macs = new - old and removed_macs = old - new from exactly two snapshots and publishes immediately. There is no 'seen absent for N consecutive cycles' gate, no per-device last-seen timestamp, and run_report() (report.py:608-652) is invoked once per discovery with no cross-run state beyond the single previous snapshot. Therefore ANY mechanism that makes a MAC absent for one cycle (DHCP lease expiry mid-walk, walker ordering change, a device powered off for a single maintenance minute) emits device_removed at once and device_added on return. The test suite (test_report.py TestMqttEvents) only asserts the raw set-difference behavior and codifies this no-debounce design as intended.
confirmed.trigger: Brief one-cycle absence of any device: short power cycle, DHCP lease churn (switch/AP 2-min leases), or a missed entry in a single discovery walk.
confirmed.consumer_symptom: NMS gets churny device_removed/device_added pairs for devices that are effectively healthy, producing spurious add/remove history in MongoDB and flapping presence indicators on the dashboard.

verdict.reasoning: The falsifiable claim is statically true. generate_device_mqtt_events() (report.py:433-456) computes added_macs = set(new_devices) - set(old_devices) and removed_macs = set(old_devices) - set(new_devices) from exactly two snapshots (self.device_instances vs self.previous_instances) and immediately calls publish_to_mqtt('obn/event/device_added'/'device_removed') inside the loop. There is NO per-device last-seen timestamp, NO 'absent for N consecutive cycles' counter, and NO rolling history: previous_instances is loaded from the single report_file snapshot (load_json, lines 83-100) and store_report() (137-141) overwrites that single file each run, so run_report() (608-652) carries no cross-run state beyond one prior snapshot. I checked every plausible upstream guard and none debounces: (a) compare_json() (102-135) only decides whether to send AT ALL — a one-cycle removal trivially passes (different size -> return True), so it enables rather than suppresses the event; (b) only_send_as_master / ospf.is_master_ccu() (637) is a master-CCU gate, orthogonal to debounce; (c) the always_publish_mqtt elif (645) republishes consist state but does NOT call generate_device_mqtt_events, so it adds nothing here; (d) no None-filter, no missing-neighbours guard on the event path. The test suite codifies the no-debounce design as intended: TestMqttEvents.test_device_removed (test_report.py:1311-1319) asserts a single absent-in-current snapshot fires device_removed exactly once; test_device_added (1300-1308) the inverse; test_empty_start (1396-1409) fires 5 adds. All green, all asserting raw set-difference with immediate publish; none asserts any confirmation/hysteresis. Verdict is confirmed for the code-level defect. The one caveat (kept from the discovery dependency) is that whether a transient absence actually reaches this diff depends on the upstream discovery path producing a partial device list rather than failing closed — that layer is outside the audited subtree — but the audited code itself has no guard, which is exactly what the claim asserts.
verdict.covered_by_test: tests/lib/report/test_report.py::TestMqttEvents (test_device_removed line 1311-1319, test_device_added 1300-1308, test_multple_removed 1336-1347, test_empty_start 1396-1409). These tests assert the raw set-difference behavior with immediate publish from a single snapshot pair and codify the no-debounce design; none asserts any confirmation/hysteresis gate.
verdict.consumer_impact: NMS (and its MongoDB device-presence history) receives a device_removed event the first time any MAC is missing from a single discovery snapshot and a paired device_added when it returns. For the ÖBB DOSTO fleet this is most likely on VDS switches and Westermo APs, which hold 2-minute DHCP leases (per CLAUDE.md) — a single missed discovery walk, a brief power cycle, or lease churn yields a spurious removed/added pair. Result: flapping presence indicators on the NMS dashboard and spurious add/remove rows in the device history for devices that are effectively healthy, with no false-alarm suppression. Scope: every commissioned train whose CCU publishes to NMS (only_send_as_master path or single-CCU); does not corrupt the consist state report itself, only the event stream.

confirmed.title: number_of_coaches derived from max(coach_number) drops trailing coaches whose devices the walk failed to number
confirmed.claim: generate_nodes() computes number_of_coaches = max(node['coach_number']) over the discovered consist (lines 44-49), then generate_coach_nodes() emits the per-coach template grid for range(1, number_of_coaches+1). The coach count is therefore bounded by the HIGHEST successfully-numbered coach. coach_number defaults to None (lib/report/device.py:23) and stays None for any device the primary topology walk could not number. If every device that belongs to the last coach fails to be numbered (one SNMP timeout on the end-of-train switch, a dead/bypassed switch, an unreachable AP), max(coach_number) falls short and the entire trailing coach is omitted from the LLD output. Zabbix then never creates discovery hosts for that coach, so all of its switches/APs silently disappear from monitoring rather than alarming as down.
confirmed.trigger: A discovery cycle where the highest-positioned coach's devices all have coach_number=None (walk miss / dead end-switch). number_of_coaches undercounts and that coach's LLD rows are never generated.
confirmed.consumer_symptom: Zabbix LLD discovers fewer coaches than the train physically has; the last coach's hosts are never created and show as absent (not as DOWN), so a real outage on the end car is invisible.

verdict.reasoning:
Cited code verified exactly at src/usr/share/obn/lib/zabbix.py:44-49: generate_nodes() sets number_of_coaches=-1 then takes max over node["coach_number"] across the discovered consist, and generate_coach_nodes() (line 57) emits the per-coach template grid for range(1, number_of_coaches+1). The coach count is therefore strictly bounded by the highest discovered coach_number. The data source is /tmp/discovery.prev.json (zabbix_generate.py:7,11), i.e. the `obn report` snapshot.

The hunter's mechanism is correct, and the real code path makes it WORSE than described, not better. coach_number defaults to None (lib/report/device.py:23, confirmed). In the DOSTO NEU walk (lib/report/report_dosto_neu.py number_coaches, BFS from the CCU), any device the walk cannot reach/number keeps coach_number=None. Crucially, line 162 calls self.normalise_devices(), which (report.py:245-260) DELETES every device with coach_number is None from device_instances before store_report() (report.py:137-141) serializes them to the snapshot. So unnumbered trailing-coach devices are not merely None in the snapshot — they are absent entirely. Either way the effect on zabbix.py:46 is identical: max() never sees them, so number_of_coaches undercounts and the entire trailing coach's LLD rows in range(1, max+1) are never generated.

No upstream guard pads the count to the physical consist length. consist.yaml (consist_map) only supplies the per-coach device template (type/device_number); it carries no independent coach count. There is no only_send_as_master gate, no None filter that raises the max, no physical-length backstop. Code at report.py:433 generate_device_mqtt_events() diffs new vs previous purely by MAC-set membership: removed_macs = set(old)-set(new); added_macs = set(new)-set(old). There is NO debounce, grace count, retry, or any distinction between 'truly gone' and 'missed this cycle'.

needs_runtime.title: generate_nodes() accesses node['coach_number'] without the key-presence guard that check() uses

needs_runtime.trigger: A discovered_consist record missing the coach_number key (partial/hand-edited discovery.prev.json, or a future serialization that omits None fields).

verdict.reasoning:

So the whole train's LLD output is lost, not one device skipped. That part of the claim holds.

But the hunter's exposure analysis is BOTH understated and overstated, and the realistic trigger is narrower than "device serialization is asdict so the key is normally present":
- Understated: device.py:23 declares `coach_number: int = field(default=None)` and as_dict() (lines 47-53) uses `skip_empty=True`, which DROPS every None field. So the dataclass asdict is the *cause* of omission, not a safeguard — any device with coach_number=None serializes WITHOUT the key. Additionally backbone_discovery.py writes raw discovery.json entries with no coach_number at all for unknown-OUI devices (line 70) and SNMP-comms-failed devices (line 82, `{"mac": dev.mac, "ip": dev.ip}`).

That writer sorts via `itemgetter("coach_number", ...)` at line 140, which would itself KeyError on a None/missing coach_number — meaning the report stage crashes FIRST on the same data, so the normal `obn report` pipeline does not deposit coach_number-less rows into prev.json. The generate-path KeyError is therefore reachable mainly via (a) a hand-edited/partial prev.json (the hunter's stated trigger), (b) pointing zabbix_generate at raw discovery.json instead of prev.json, or (c) a future change to store_report serialization. It is real but data/runtime-dependent, not provable as a default-pipeline crash.

No upstream None/missing-key filter exists in generate_nodes() or zabbix_generate.py. The contract mismatch between the two classes is genuine and unguarded on the generate side.

refuted.title: device_removed/device_added/device_changed payloads drop fields via skip_empty as_dict(), shipping shape-incomplete events
refuted.claim: All three event payloads serialize with Device.as_dict() (report.py:442, 448, 455), and as_dict() defaults skip_empty=True (device.py:47-53), dropping every key whose value is None or []. A device_removed event for a comm-failed device (only mac+ip survived discovery) therefore carries no type/coach_number/device_number, and a device_changed event whose change was a field going to None simply omits that key rather than signaling it cleared. Unlike obn/consist (create_nms_device_nodes, which substitutes 'unknown' and fixed keys, report.py:206-214), the event topics emit a variable-shape dict with no type/coach guarantee. NMS consuming obn/event/device_* cannot reliably index removed/changed devices by coach/type/device-number.

refuted.consumer_symptom: NMS receives device_added/removed/changed events missing the type/coach/device-number it needs to correlate the event to a diagram position - the event cannot be reconciled against the consist, so the inventory update is dropped or misattributed.

The mechanism is real but the consumer-symptom is guarded out. Confirmed facts: report.py:442/448/455 serialize device_added/removed/changed via Device.as_dict() (new_devices[mac] for added/changed, old_devices[mac] for removed), and device.py:47-53 defaults skip_empty=True, dropping every key whose value is None or []. So the payloads ARE variable-shape and an optional field that goes to None (e.g. firmware/config/serial) is omitted rather than emitted as null — that narrow part is true.

But the headline claim — that NMS cannot index events by coach/type/device-number — is refuted by an upstream guard.
